rv.q: Emma Bailey’s set is a dune of bleached-white sand, clumps of sea grass forcing their way through into a scorched environment, baked by Colin Grenfell’s lighting.

Redmond delivers Winnie’s lines with a see-saw vocal cadence that includes a regular falsetto yelp that is both endearing and infuriating. Yet behind that inane delivery lie hints of insecurity and vulnerability.
Vivid staging of Beckett’s sand-bound two-hander

Instead, the production focuses on the beating, vulnerable heart of the text. What shines through the sundered landscape is a fierce, defiant song of survival – a monumental theatrical achievement that proves even when we are up to our necks in the sand, the human spirit refuses to be silenced.

No sexual fulfilment = resort to pornography. Beckett’s Absurdist Routine: Finding Meaning in the Minutiae Back to Winnie and her ramblings. She is doing her utmost to keep herself amused, despite her boredom with the unrelenting daily routine – yes, you can see where this is going – so every little distraction is a pleasure.
